deep.reconstruction:
This page is the blue archival cover, or wrapper, of the bundle Cod. Ms. Riemann 6 in the Göttingen Riemann Nachlass. It contains no mathematics.

What is on the page:
(a) Upper left, in ink, a librarian's shelfmark: 'Cod. Ms. Riemann 6'.
(b) Upper right, a printed decorative label filled in by hand. It reads 'Lineare Differenzial Gleichungen' (Linear Differential Equations). Below this is '6.', partly struck through with a blue pencil stroke, and the Roman numeral 'XVI'. The numeral is probably an older ordering number from the arrangement of the Nachlass, made by the family, Dedekind or Weber.
(c) Near the top centre, a faint red pencil note. It is probably an archival leaf count; it seems to begin '28 Bl.' (Blätter), followed by further abbreviated characters I cannot read reliably.

What the label indicates: the enclosed folios concern linear differential equations. This is the topic of Riemann's published 1857 memoir on the Gauss hypergeometric series, 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen'. It is also the topic of his unpublished 1857 fragment on linear differential equations with algebraic coefficients, 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten'. That fragment was published posthumously in the Werke (1876) and anticipates the Riemann–Hilbert problem. This identification is an inference from the label only; nothing on this page itself can be checked.

There are no derivations to reconstruct.
deep.surprise_reason: This is an archival cover sheet with only a shelfmark, a subject label and an archival leaf-count note. It contains no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: The '6.' on the label is partly crossed out with a blue pencil stroke.
'Gleichungen' on the label is written in Kurrent script, roughly as 'Gleichungen'; the reading is correct.
The faint red note near the top centre appears to begin '28 Bl.', probably an archival leaf count (Blätter); the remainder is illegible.
